messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: GPU queue growth detected for private VPC cluster 'cust-acme-west' (region: us-west-2). Severity: P1. Alert rule: private.cluster.queue.size > 150 for 3m. @maya assigned :rotating_light:

maya: I'm on it. Paging @samg as primary oncall and @jonp for customer impact.

samg: seeing the alert, joining. quick health check: 
- queue length: 312
- age p95: 7m12s
- backend errors: 480s of "no capacity" from allocator

jonp: customer-jones just DM'd support that latency jumped and started getting OOMs in user jobs. total affected customers: 1 tenant (cust-acme).

priyarao: can we confirm autoscaler activity? looks like it's requesting nodes but new nodes aren't Ready.

leo: i'm attaching current node state: 
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=cluster=cust-acme-west
NAME                                        STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-0-5-12.us-west-2.compute.internal     NotReady   <none>   2m    v1.26.3
ip-10-0-6-34.us-west-2.compute.internal     NotReady   <none>   3m    v1.26.3
ip-10-0-7-21.us-west-2.compute.internal     Pending    <none>   1m    
```

infra-bot: autoscaler logs show API errors: 
```
E0901 12:41:02 provider.go:312] CreateNodeGroup failed: RequestLimitExceeded: Request limit exceeded.
	status code: 429, request id: abc-123
```

samg: that 429 to cloud API explains slow node bootstrap. nodes are stuck in provisioning; image pulls are backlogged. looks like customer VPC has strict egress NAT capacity so we can't pull images fast.

maya: customer has a private VPC with limited NAT gateways, right? cust-acme confirmed they have an internal security policy that blocks some egress and they rely on our node bootstrap to pull images through an internal proxy.

jonp: customer-impact summary for execs: "Cust-acme production model serving degraded; requests are queuing and some inference jobs returned 503. Estimated affected requests: ~18k in last 10m."

priyarao: immediate mitigations we can do: 
1) Failover some routing to regional shared-hosted pool (requires tenant routing flip).
2) Increase autoscaler timeout/backoff and retry create calls (but cloud 429 will still throttle).
3) Ask infra to manually create pre-warmed instances in the customer's subnet (needs cust permission).

leo: trying a manual scale via kube provisioner: 
```
# create 2 spot-safe instances in cust subnet (manual step, only if approved)
aws ec2 run-instances --subnet-id subnet-0abc --image-id ami-XXXXX --count 2 --instance-type g4dn.xlarge --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=cluster,Value=cust-acme-west}]'
```

infra-bot: note: manual instance creation will likely hit the same API rate limits if there are many concurrent ops. Could stagger requests.

support-bot: notified customer-jones that we're investigating and may perform a routing failover; customer requested we announce before any failover.

customer-jones: please don't move traffic without our signoff. we can approve warm-up nodes in 30m if that helps.

samg: plan A (fast, with customer approval): request cust signoff to allow us to create 2 pre-warmed nodes in their VPC, staggered. estimate 20–30m to Ready.

maya: Plan B (no cust approval): start tenant routing to shared regional pool (will preserve isolation via tenant namespaces) — needs product/ops handshake, risk: some models may be on only-customer optimized images. need a fallback image.

jonp: set up a routing toggle. @priyarao can you coordinate with eng-runtime to ensure fallback image exists?

priyarao: on it. if fallback image not available we may return soft-degraded responses with warning headers.

leo: meanwhile i'm increasing kubelet image pull backoff and cleaning up Pending nodes to free resources: 
```
kubectl delete node ip-10-0-7-21.us-west-2.compute.internal || true
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-6-34.us-west-2.compute.internal && kubectl drain ip-10-0-6-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

samg: doing a cautious routing failover test to 10% traffic to hosted pool to measure latency and correctness.

incident-bot: Change event: routing-toggle set to 10% -> hosted region-us-west-shared at 12:48 UTC by samg.

maya: 10% ramp looks fine for now, no new errors observed on shared pool. queue dropped from 312 to 240 in 5m.

customer-jones: ok we authorize creation of 2 nodes, but please keep failover at <=30% until new nodes are Ready.

leo: starting node creation now (stagger 60s).

infra-bot: manual node create accepted; note that image proxy error still seen: "xfer timeout to proxy" for one node. retrying.

samg: new nodes reached Ready at 13:08 UTC, adding them to cluster. queue dropped to 86, p95 1m20s.

maya: good. switching routing back to 0% hosted (full traffic to customer cluster) per customer request and now that customer nodes are Ready.

incident-bot: Change event: routing-toggle set to 0% at 13:12 UTC by maya.

jonp: notify customer success for post-incident comms and set expectation for root cause analysis.

support-bot: customer notified: "We're stabilizing your cluster and will follow up with RCA and timeline for preventing recurrence."

priyarao: immediate action items (assigned): 
- infra: investigate cloud API 429 spike and request limit quarters (leo)
- runtime: add autoscaler jitter and exponential backoff tuning (priyarao)
- devex: document safe routing failover steps and checklist (maya)
- support: confirm customer approval flow for manual node creation (jonp)

maya: handing off to night oncall @samg for follow-up and RCA. I'll draft the incident ticket.

samg: taking it. will link logs, timeline, and mitigation steps. handing to next oncall at 23:00 UTC if not closed.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged and assigned to samg.

maya: nice work team. please keep notes in the incident board and add any config snippets used. :white_check_mark:

customer-jones: thanks for quick response. our ops team will open a ticket to increase NAT capacity too.

leo: saving logs to /var/lib/incident-logs/2301112222-cust-acme-west.log and will attach to the ticket.

priyarao: postmortem owners: priyarao (runtime), leo (infra). ETA: 72 hours.

samg: closing thread here; will update incident ticket and ping channel when RCA published.
